slot.brief: A train moves toward then away from a stationary observer sounding a whistle; compare apparent frequencies for approach and recession using the Doppler formula.

stem: A train moving toward and then away from a stationary observer sounds a whistle of frequency $f$. If the train's speed is $20$ m s$^{-1}$ and the speed of sound is $340$ m s$^{-1}$, what is the ratio of the apparent frequency on approach to that on recession?

verdicts.working: For a moving source and stationary observer, the approach frequency is $f_a=f\,340/(340-20)=17f/16$; the recession frequency is $f_r=f\,340/(340+20)=17f/18$. Thus $f_a/f_r=9/8$.

working:
$f_{\text{app}}=f\dfrac{v}{v-v_s}$ on approach; $f_{\text{rec}}=f\dfrac{v}{v+v_s}$ on recession.
$\dfrac{f_{\text{app}}}{f_{\text{rec}}}=\dfrac{340+20}{340-20}=\dfrac{360}{320}=\dfrac{9}{8}$

Independent check: For a moving source and stationary observer, the approach frequency is $f_a=f\,340/(340-20)=17f/16$; the recession frequency is $f_r=f\,340/(340+20)=17f/18$. Thus $f_a/f_r=9/8$.
solution:
For a moving source and stationary observer, $f_a=f\dfrac{v}{v-v_s}$ and $f_r=f\dfrac{v}{v+v_s}$. Thus
$$\frac{f_a}{f_r}=\frac{v+v_s}{v-v_s}=\frac{340+20}{340-20}=\frac{9}{8}.$$
